A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HAMSTER and contain readable methods, equations, results, figures, and Appendices A–G. Relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original real-robot experiments, Colosseum simulations, human evaluations of predicted paths, and ablation results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds HAMSTER results on general vision-language benchmarks in Table 4.

M1.justification: The VILA-based path predictor, path simplification, RVT2/3D-DA controllers, training objectives, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Concatenated path channels and the alternative model sizes already appeared in v1.

E1.justification: v4 substantially extends evaluation beyond robot execution and path prediction to general vision-language tasks, including VQAv2, GQA, VizWiz, ScienceQA-IMG, TextVQA, Chinese MMBench, and MMMU. Table 4 contains 14 benchmark columns, although the prose says 15. Existing training and robotics coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds the base VILA1.5-13B as an explicit comparator against HAMSTER. The OpenVLA, RVT2, 3D-DA, and GPT-4o/Code-as-Policies comparisons remain; the RLBench-finetuned OpenVLA control is relocated, not newly introduced.

E3.justification: The added VQA comparison introduces controls matching HAMSTER and VILA1.5-13B on their LLM and image resolution. Existing robotics evaluation budgets, camera trials, and Appendix G settings are unchanged. Detailed prompting and scoring procedures for the new benchmarks are not supplied.

E4.justification: The new base-model comparison explicitly probes retention of general VLM capabilities after fine-tuning. Appendix G also replaces Figure 17's jar-closing examples while retaining the RDP-versus-20-point comparison, model sizes, protocol, and conclusions. Earlier robustness, data-efficiency, and failure analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five-seed simulation evaluation and the same uncertainty-bearing table entries. The new VQA table supplies point estimates without adding repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds a substantial set of vision-language results: for example, HAMSTER versus base VILA scores are 64.9 versus 64.3 on GQA and 61.4 versus 65.0 on TextVQA. Figure 17 substitutes different qualitative trajectory predictions. All retained numerical tables match after renumbering; these additions do not establish improved robotics performance from v1 to v4.

T1.justification: The path definitions and likelihood-based training formulations are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical results or proofs that are added, removed, or revised in the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: hierarchical path guidance enables off-domain training and improved robotic generalization. The principal OpenVLA improvement claims remain unchanged; the new VQA evidence does not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: v4 interprets Table 4 as evidence that HAMSTER remains a general-purpose VLM. It also proposes that concatenated channels preserve paths that RVT2 reprojection might fragment, extending the existing reprojection discussion in Appendix E. The stated 2D-interface and dynamic-environment limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table 4 newly documents matched LLM/image resolution and describes HAMSTER as trained 'without curated vision-language finetuning.' This adds a brief technical characterization without establishing a changed training recipe. Existing data processing, prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, training time, and access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of track-any-point and object-trajectory approaches, including Track2Act and General Flow, and considers extending HAMSTER beyond end-effector paths. Benchmark references and some background citations are added or changed, while the central positioning relative to monolithic VLAs and RT-Trajectory remains.

P1.justification: Section 5 is reorganized around Q1–Q5: the OpenVLA control moves into the real-world evaluation, data efficiency into simulation evaluation, and Section 5.3 focuses on VLM generalization. There are localized wording edits, while the overall document structure, methods, and appendices remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 4, reformats Figure 4's chart and legend, replaces Figure 17's illustrated examples, and relocates the task montage from main-text Figure 7 to appendix Figure 8. Other figures and tables are resized, moved, or renumbered without a wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful direct evidence about retention of general VLM capabilities, which v1 mainly motivated through its co-training design, and broadens the related-work discussion. The gain is limited: robotics evidence is unchanged, the new benchmark results are mixed, evaluation details are sparse, and the stated 15 benchmarks do not match Table 4's 14 columns.
